title: Strict-local sections meet dense opens after any fibre field extension
statement: Let $A$ be a nonzero commutative Noetherian strictly henselian local ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring, def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology], put $S=\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], and let $p:Y\to S$ be a smooth surjective finite-type morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. A section is a morphism $a:S\to Y$ with $p\circ a=\mathrm{id}_S$. Then $Y(S)\ne\varnothing$. Moreover, for every point $s\in S$, every field extension $L/\kappa(s)$ [def-weil-residue-field, def-pc-field-extension], and every dense open $O\subseteq Y_L=Y\times_S\operatorname{Spec}L$ [def-pc-base-change], there is a section $a\in Y(S)$ whose induced $L$-point belongs to $O$. No geometric irreducibility, connectedness, fixed relative dimension, or chosen section is assumed.

source.place: 2.3 Proposition 5, printed p.47 (PDF p.53); 5.3 Lemma 7, printed pp.126-127 (PDF pp.132-133), and the field-extension paragraph in the proof of Lemma 6, printed pp.125-126 (PDF pp.131-132), citing EGA IV_3 11.10.7; primary scan read at https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/~kamenova/homepage_files/Bosch_Raynaud_Neron_Model_tc.pdf; local PDF WANTED.

proof.text: Write $s_0$ for the closed point and $k=\kappa(s_0)$. The field $k$ is separably closed by [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology]. The fibre $Y_k$ is nonempty by surjectivity and [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-base-change], and smooth by [lem-pc-proper-base-change]. By [lem-pc-dense-separable-points] its closed points with finite separable residue field are dense, so choose one, $y$; its residue field is $k$. Apply [lem-sfb-smooth-space-dimension-strata] to the scheme $Y$, viewed as an algebraic space with its identity chart. The relative dimension stratum containing $y$ is open and has some dimension $n\geq0$. Choose an affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}B$ of $Y$ containing $y$ inside that stratum. Its map to $S$ is smooth by [lem-pc-open-immersion-smooth-composition]. Since source and target are affine, [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-iff-smooth-affine] says $B$ is a smooth, hence finitely presented and finite type, $A$-algebra.

source.place: 5.3 Lemma 7, reduction to constant relative dimension; 2.3 Proposition 5; Stacks 056U (varieties-lemma-smooth-separable-closed-points-dense) and 02G1 (morphisms-lemma-smooth-omega-finite-locally-free).

proof.text: For every $b\in U_k(k)$ its affine-coordinate map $B\to k=A/\mathfrak m$ lifts to an $A$-algebra map $B\to A$ by [lem-trf-henselian-smooth-algebra-lifting], taking its $R=A$, smooth algebra $S=B$, target algebra $A$, and ideal $I=\mathfrak m$. The maximal-ideal pair is henselian by [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology]. Thus reduction $U(S)\to U_k(k)$ is onto. The fibre $U_k=U\times_S\operatorname{Spec}k$ is smooth over $k$ as a base change of the smooth $U\to S$ of step 1 [lem-pc-proper-base-change], so the same separable-point density lemma applied to $U_k$ shows that the values at $s_0$ of all sections $a\in U(S)$ are dense in $U_k$. In particular one such section exists, and composition with $U\hookrightarrow Y$ proves $Y(S)\ne\varnothing$.

For $t\in S$ put $D_t=\{a(t):a\in U(S)\}$ and $C_t=\overline{D_t}\subseteq U_t$. Since $S$ is local, each $t$ specializes to $s_0$. Apply [lem-sfb-section-value-closure-dimension-specialization] to $A,B$, the family of all sections of $U$, and $(t_1,t_0)=(t,s_0)$. It gives $\dim C_t\geq\dim C_{s_0}=\dim U_k$. The strata lemma makes every point of every $U_t$ have local fibre dimension $n$; its base-change clause also applies to these ordinary fibres. These are affine finite type schemes over fields, hence Noetherian with finitely many components by [lem-wf-affine-noetherian-components]. By [lem-sbc-constant-local-dimension-components] each component has dimension $n$. Consequently a nonempty $U_t$ has dimension $n$: any irreducible closed chain is contained in a component, and the dimension of each component is $n$. Thus $\dim U_k=n$, $\dim C_t\geq n$, and in particular $U_t$ is nonempty and has dimension $n$.

source.place: 5.3 Lemma 7, first assertion and constant-dimension argument; Stacks 02G1 and 02G2.

proof.text: Fix the point $s$ and extension $L/\kappa(s)$ of the statement. The closed subset $C_s$ has dimension at least $n$ in the nonempty Noetherian scheme $U_s$ of dimension $n$. By [lem-sc-hilbert-nowhere-dense-dimension-drop] it cannot be nowhere dense. Since it is closed, its interior $V=\operatorname{Int}_{U_s}(C_s)$ is therefore a nonempty open of $U_s$. The subset $D_s\cap V$ is dense in $V$: every nonempty open of $V$ is an open of $U_s$ contained in $C_s=\overline{D_s}$, so meets $D_s$. Each of these rational points factors uniquely through $V$ by [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-factors-through-open-subscheme]. Apply [lem-sfb-rational-density-field-extension] to the scheme $V$ over $\kappa(s)$ and this specified subset of rational points. Their induced $L$-points are dense in $V_L$.

source.place: 11.10.7, applied after taking the nonempty interior supplied by the BLR 5.3 Lemma 7 dimension bound.

proof.text: The open immersions $V\hookrightarrow U_s\hookrightarrow Y_s$ remain open immersions after extension to $L$ by [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-base-change], so $V_L$ is open in $Y_L$. It is nonempty: [lem-pc-field-extension-surjective] and [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-base-change] make $V_L\to V$ surjective. The dense open $O\subseteq Y_L$ therefore meets $V_L$ in a nonempty open. The density proved in step 4 gives a section $a\in U(S)$ with $a(s)\in V$ and $a_L\in O\cap V_L$. Compose $a$ with $U\hookrightarrow Y$. Its composite with $p$ is still $\mathrm{id}_S$, and its induced $L$-point is the one just selected, by the defining projection equalities of base change. This proves the required assertion for every $s,L,O$.

source.place: 5.3 proof of Lemma 6, printed pp.125–126 (PDF pp.131–132), dense-open conclusion of the field-extension paragraph.

EGA IV_3 Cor. 11.10.7 (printed p.172) was read locally. BLR is not in literature/ (the report says WANTED, and proof_origin is agent), so I checked the BLR-based steps independently. The statement is unchanged and true. Step 1: strictly henselian means the residue field is separably closed; the separable closed points of the smooth closed fibre (Stacks 056U) are therefore k-rational; the smooth-space strata are used with the identity chart, and only the clopen strata are used; an affine chart is chosen inside one stratum. Step 2: Stacks 0H74 is applied with (A,m) a henselian pair, so U(S) maps onto U_k(k). Step 3: the new dimension inequality with t specializing to s0 (S is local), constant local dimension, finitely many components, so dim U_t = n and U_t is nonempty. Step 4: the nowhere-dense dimension-drop gives C_s a nonempty interior V, and the new density lemma is applied on V. Step 5: open-immersion base change and surjectivity give a nonempty V_L that meets O. New node lem-sfb-section-value-closure-dimension-specialization is true: reduce to a DVR (Stacks 054F); the flat closure Z̄ of the generic closure contains every a_i(s), and dim Z̄_s ≤ dim Z_eta. Tested on x=ct over k[t] (generic dimension 1, special dimension 0) and on an empty family. New node lem-sfb-rational-density-field-extension is true for arbitrary k-schemes: in the affine case, write f = Σ r_j⊗l_j with the l_j independent; vanishing on D_L makes each r_j nilpotent. This matches EGA 11.10.7. Duplicates: cor-pc-dense-points-curves-sections (1) needs a separably closed base and all of X(k), and lem-sfb-dense-rational-closed-subscheme-descent is a different statement; no node states the dimension inequality, and neither new node restates the item. Batch-5: lem-sfb-smooth-space-dimension-strata reaches def-trf-algebraic-space only as a general definition, and lem-trf-henselian-smooth-algebra-lifting is general commutative algebra (0H74); neither is a step of the trace formula or of Poincaré duality, so both are accepted. Tool uses accepted.
